title: How the Amount Left With the Policyholder Falls Across the Lines Outside Cover
content:
What is left with the policyholder on a policy under Medicare Supplement Insurance Policies falls across the lines outside cover, and how many times it is taken depends on what those lines are.

1. Where more than one line falls outside cover and each was a visit of its own, what is left with the policyholder falls on each of those lines separately.
2. Where lines fall outside cover and belong to one Medicare claim, what is left with the policyholder falls once on each such claim.
3. Where neither of those holds, it is not applied at all, no line falling outside cover.

### The difference between the first two

The first case requires both that more than one line falls outside cover and that each of those lines was a visit of its own. The amount is then taken as many times as there are lines.

The second case applies where the lines outside cover belong to one Medicare claim, and the amount is taken once for each such claim rather than once for each line. Several lines of one claim therefore bear the amount once between them.

### Hypothetical counts

Three lines fall outside cover and each was a visit of its own, and what is left with the policyholder is 50.00: the amount falls on each of the 3 lines separately, giving 150.00.

Four lines fall outside cover and they belong to 2 Medicare claims, and what is left with the policyholder is 50.00: the amount falls once on each of those 2 claims, giving 100.00.

No line falls outside cover: the amount is not applied at all.
